CONDUCTION IN HETEROGENEOUS MEDIA.
[310.
functions of the derivatives of $V$, the forms of which are given
in the equations
$$\left.\begin{array}{rl}
u & =r_{1} X+p_{3} Y+q_{2} Z, \\
v & =q_{3} X+r_{2} Y+p_{1} Z, \\
w & =p_{2} X+q_{1} Y+r_{3} Z,
\end{array}\right\}$$
(3)
where $X, Y, Z$ are the derivatives of $V$ with respect to $x, y, z$
respectively.
Let us take the case of the surface which separates a medium
having these coefficients of conduction from an isotropic medium
having a coefficient of conduction equal to $r$.
Let $X^{\prime}, Y^{\prime}, Z^{\prime}$ be the values of $X, Y, Z$ in the isotropic medium,
then we have at the surface
$$\begin{array}{lc}
V & =V^{\prime} \\
\text { or } & X d x+Y d y+Z d z=X^{\prime} d x+Y^{\prime} d y+Z^{\prime} d z, \\
\text { when } & l d x+m d y+n d z=0 .
\end{array}$$
(4)
(5)
(6)
This condition leads to
$$X^{\prime}=X+4 \pi \sigma l, \quad Y^{\prime}=Y+4 \pi \sigma m, \quad Z^{\prime}=Z+4 \pi \sigma n,$$
(7)
where $\sigma$ is the surface-density.
We have also in the isotropic medium
$$u^{\prime}=r X^{\prime}, \quad v^{\prime}=r Y^{\prime}, \quad w^{\prime}=r Z^{\prime},$$
(8)
and at the boundary the condition of flow is
$$u^{\prime} l+v^{\prime} m+w^{\prime} n=u l+v m+w n,$$
(9)
or $r(l X+m Y+n Z+4 \pi \sigma)$
$=l\left(r_{1} X+p_{3} Y+q_{2} Z\right)+m\left(q_{3} X+r_{2} Y+p_{1} Z\right)+n\left(p_{2} X+q_{1} Y+r_{3} Z\right)$,
(10)
whence
$$\begin{aligned}
4 \pi \sigma r=\left\{l\left(r_{1}-r\right)+m q_{3}+n p_{2}\right\} X+ & \left\{l p_{3}+m\left(r_{2}-r\right)+n q_{1}\right\} Y \\
& +\left\{l q_{2}+m p_{1}+n\left(r_{3}-r\right)\right\} Z
\end{aligned}$$
(11)
The quantity $\sigma$ represents the surface-density of the charge
on the surface of separation. In crystallized and organized sub-
stances it depends on the direction of the surface as well as on
the force perpendicular to it. In isotropic substances the coeffi-
cients $p$ and $q$ are zero, and the coefficients $r$ are all equal,
so that
$$4 \pi \sigma=\left(\frac{r_{1}}{r}-1\right)(l X+m Y+n Z)$$
(12)
where $r_{1}$ is the conductivity of the substance, $r$ that of the
external medium, and $l, m, n$ the direction-cosines of the normal
drawn towards the medium whose conductivity is $r$.
When both media are isotropic the conditions may be greatly
simplified, for if $k$ is the specific resistance per unit of volume,
